title: ResultEnvelope
description: The standard output envelope used only when the effective output kind is `RESULT_ENVELOPE`, and by every `apply` op (CLI-SPEC §3b). Resolve an invocation's effective kind from its matching profile: matching `operationalProfiles[].returns.views[]` overrides `operationalProfiles[].returns.kind`; without a matching view, use that primary kind. `RAW_JSON`, `RAW_TEXT`, `EMPTY_STDOUT`, and `NDJSON_STREAM` emit an artifact/catalog value, a rendered view, no stdout, or a newline-delimited stream of protocol frames instead, so this schema does not apply to those outputs. THREE ORTHOGONAL AXES, never conflated: `ok` = the operation succeeded (ordinary `batch` follows every child exit; `batch --observations` follows full dispatch plus artifact write); `valid` = the subject model is kernel-valid (a consistency VERDICT, so it appears only where a gate produced one); `verification`/`engine` = who vouches for it. A read that succeeded is `ok:true` and carries NO `valid`, because it established no verdict. Optional keys are omitted when not applicable, and WHICH may appear is decided by what the invocation actually did, never by which verb it was. TWO KINDS OF ADDRESS ride an envelope, and a coordinate-free one is NOT a declaration: a model-ELEMENT path (a declaration, such as `diagnostics[].where.path`, `where.rule`, or a runtime payload's `declaration`) always carries a LEADING SLASH, while a document CELL address is A12's canonical instance pointer, which has NO leading slash and OMITS `[1]`, so `Order/Lines/LineTotal` under a runtime `field` names repetition 1 of every level, spelled identically to the declaration it is not. Runtime payload keys state which contract they keep with a `format`: `a12-pointer` is always canonical, `a12-message-address` is canonical exactly when the address names ONE cell and is otherwise the interpreter's house form (leading slash, every level's index spelled: `/Order[1]/Lines[0]/LineTotal`), because A12 defines no pointer string for a message address carrying a wildcard or an unresolved level. That rule is decided PER ADDRESS, not per key, so one message legitimately shows both spellings, a `field` that hit one row beside a `referenced` operand that is a whole column. Test the leading slash to tell them apart; the per-key contracts are in `schema model eval` / `schema model compute` / `schema rule eval`.

target.description: the element family acted on: model | rule | computation | field | group | typedef | include | config | workspace | patterns | profile | where-used | meta

op.description: the operation: add | read | modify | remove | validate | check | explain | describe | export | eval | compute | compare | scaffold | …

outcome.description: the execution result class; `error` = the tool itself failed (an unexpected throwable caught at the boundary, exit 70), distinct from `rejected` (input rejected, exit 1). `read` covers EVERY non-mutating result class, including a query, verdict, runtime observation, or comparison, so `outcome` alone does not tell you whether `valid` may be present. For `batch`, `completed` means every child was dispatched. Inspect `data.allExitedZero` and each child's exact exit. Ordinary batch sets outer `ok` false and exits 1 when any child exits nonzero. Observation batch sets outer `ok` true and exits 0 after full dispatch plus artifact write, independently of `allExitedZero`. Batch is non-transactional, so an earlier successful write remains. Contrast `apply`, whose ops are steps of ONE transaction and roll back together

ok.description: the operation succeeded. True for applied | preview | read | staged. For completed ordinary batch dispatch, true only when `data.allExitedZero` is true. For completed observation batch, true when every child was dispatched and the artifact was written, independently of `data.allExitedZero`. False for an ordinary completed batch with any nonzero child, an observation artifact write failure, and refused | rejected | error

valid.description: the subject model is kernel-valid — a consistency VERDICT, distinct from `ok`. PRESENT ONLY on a genuine verdict (`model check`, `rule check`, `workspace check`, a `patterns` scaffold review) and on a rejection the kernel gate produced (then `false`). ABSENT on every read, runtime evaluation, comparison, mutation, refusal, and pre-flight rejection — none of those establishes a verdict. A per-entry `valid` nested inside `data` (`workspace list --validate`, `workspace check`) is a different, model-scoped fact and never affects the exit code

verification.description: how a consistency gate arbitrated THIS invocation: KERNEL_CONFIRMED = a kernel backend ran the gate (the CLI always bundles one); STRUCTURAL_ONLY = the gate ran with NO backend, so a verdict beside it reflects structural prechecks only and must not be read as kernel-green (a library-consumer posture). PRESENT on every invocation that actually ran the gate — including a `rejected` one, because KERNEL_CONFIRMED means the kernel ARBITRATED, not that the model was valid, and including a WRITE, since an edit verb gates before it writes. ABSENT when no gate ran. It is therefore per-INVOCATION and never per-verb: `model report` carries it while `model report --tree` does not, and `field add` carries it while `model normalize` (a pure reformat) does not, because only the former of each pair puts the model through the gate. On a `--dry-run` preview it answers the question `written:false` cannot: nothing was written, but the change WAS checked

engine.description: (runtime evaluation only) which implementation produced the semantic observation. `model eval`/`model compute`/`rule eval` evaluate through the kernel-free DM_INTERPRETER. Orthogonal to `verification`: an evaluation yields observations, not a verdict, so a runtime envelope carries `engine` and never `valid`

engineVersion.description: (with `engine`) the build of the engine that computed the observation — the `:interpreter` release for DM_INTERPRETER, the kernel actually on the classpath (never the built-against pin) for A12_KERNEL

toolVersion.description: (with `engine`) the `dmtool` build that projected and serialized the observation. Emitted alongside `engineVersion` rather than inferred from it: evaluation semantics can move in the engine while pointer spelling, summaries, or envelope shape move independently in the tool, so one version cannot identify what produced a retained result

summary.description: one human-readable line (the agent's quick read / log line)

changed.description: (mutations) the delta on success — e.g. {added, kind}, a refactor's rewritten references

data.description: (reads/queries/verdicts/comparisons) the op's payload — explanation tree, model card, fired-list, per-model verdicts, a profile comparison, …; shape is op-specific (see `schema <target> <op>`)

diagnostics.description: structured findings — see `schema diagnostic`. NOT A DEFECT COUNT, in either direction: the list is neither a complete enumeration of what is wrong nor one entry per problem. A rule carrying two independent defects can return ONE diagnostic (the consistency gate suppresses the other), and a single defect can return TWO (the same problem under two `MVK_*` code names). Which objection wins is not a fixed order — measured both ways. So read a lone diagnostic as AN objection, never THE objection: to attribute a refusal to a specific gate, remove the other candidate defect and re-run. A precheck refusal (`RK_*`, `source: PRECHECK`) additionally means the kernel gate was never asked, so no `MVK_*` can appear beside it however many kernel-level defects the input also carries.

written.description: whether this invocation wrote its selected model or artifact destination to disk

output.description: the path of the model or artifact destination written by this invocation; absent when `written:false`

diagnostics.summary: /Order/DeliveryDate is referenced by 1 element(s); removing it would dangle them
diagnostics.fix: pass --cascade to remove the referrers too, or remove them first

diagnostics.summary: At 'Abs'It is not allowed to use constants.
diagnostics.fix: wrap a field or an expression, not an immediate literal
